## How the economy works

Full write-up: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md`. Every number is an admin setting.

**What a token is worth:** 1 token = $0.002 of the AI cost the build service actually measures. Yakko builds are charged 1.25x. Any build that reached the AI costs at least 5 tokens.

**Tokens per typical build**, from real builds:

| Model | Typical | Bigger build |
|---|---|---|
| Katara | ~34 | ChunkMirror: 80 |
| Saka | ~52 | complex: ~95; on the current Saka model setting (Sonnet 5): 150–338 |
| Yakko | ~214 (simple) | complex: ~740 (estimate) |

**Game-server tokens.** On purchase: `clamp(round5(100 + 16 × $/mo), 150, 750)`. On each paid renewal: `clamp(round5(25 + 6 × $/mo), 40, 300)`.

| Server price | On purchase | Each renewal |
|---|---|---|
| $4.99/mo | 180 | +55 |
| $8.99/mo | 245 | +80 |
| $9.99/mo | 260 | +85 |
| $30/mo | 580 | +205 |

- A ~$10 server gets 260 tokens, and ChunkMirror on Katara costs 80, so well over half is left (a test pins this).
- Prepaid terms earn the monthly amount for each month, up to 12 months.
- These tokens expire after 90 days.
- A $0 trial gets its first grant on its first paid renewal.

**Plans**, renewing monthly, each paid month adding its tokens on top:

| Plan | Price | Tokens/month | Models | Margin if every token is used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Katara | $4.99 | 750 | Katara | $3.05 (61%) |
| Saka | $19.99 | 3,500 | Katara, Saka | $12.11 (61%) |
| All models | $49.99 | 10,000 | all three | $28.24 (56%) |

- **Stacking:** each month's plan tokens last 3 months, so at most 3 months stack.
- **Upgrade:** charged now for the rest of the month, models unlock now, tokens granted in proportion to what was paid.
- **Downgrade:** takes effect at the next renewal, no refund.
- **Cancel:** keeps the plan to the end of the paid month; its tokens then stay usable 30 days, Katara only.
- **Failed renewal:** models stay unlocked 3 days past the period end while Stripe retries.
- **Refund:** takes back that payment's unspent tokens, in proportion to the refund.

**Top-ups (I recommend offering them):** 120 tokens per $1, from $5 to $100, valid 12 months, unlock no models. Plans give more tokens per dollar, so they stay the better deal. A $10 top-up keeps about 70% margin.

**Model access:** without a plan, Katara only.

**Failed builds and limits:**
- A failure on our side is free up to 3 per rolling 7 days, then charged at actual cost.
- Refused and cancelled builds pay what they actually cost.
- Spend cap: 5,000 tokens a day, 1,000 for accounts younger than 7 days.
- To stop accounts farming tokens with cheap servers: at most 3 purchase grants per account per 30 days, and at most 3,000 unspent server tokens held.

**Worst case per customer:**
- One $8.99 server: $0.49 of AI cost the first month, $0.16 a month after.
- Anyone: at most $10 of AI cost a day.
- If a build costs more than the account holds, the balance never goes below zero; Nxeon absorbs the difference. The build service's own $4-per-build cap limits how big that can get.

- Upgrade: charged the prorated difference now, unlocked now, with tokens granted for what was paid.
- Downgrade: takes effect at the next renewal.
- Cancel: takes effect at the end of the paid month; the tokens then stay usable for 30 days on Katara only.
- Failed renewal: models stay unlocked for 3 more days while Stripe retries.
- Refund: removes that payment's unspent tokens, in proportion to the amount refunded.

**Top-ups (I recommend offering them):** 120 tokens per $1, from $5 to $100, valid for 12 months, no model unlocks. That's a worse rate than every plan, so plans stay the better deal; a $10 top-up has about a 70% margin.

**Model access without a plan:** Katara only.

**Failures and limits:**
- Failures on our side are free up to 3 per 7 days, then charged at actual cost.
- Refused and cancelled builds pay their actual cost.
- Daily spend cap: 5,000 tokens (1,000 for accounts under 7 days old).
- Anti-farming: at most 3 purchase grants per account per 30 days, and at most 3,000 unspent server tokens per account.

**Worst case:**
- An $8.99 server costs Nxeon at most $0.49 of AI in the first month and $0.16 a month after.
- No account can spend more than $10 of AI in a day.
- If a build costs more than the account has, the balance stops at zero and Nxeon absorbs the difference. The build service's $4-per-build cap bounds that.

## What's built

- **Database (additive only):** five new models: `CyrusTokenAccount`, `CyrusTokenLot`, `CyrusTokenLedger` (append-only, each entry has a unique key so nothing applies twice), `CyrusTokenReservation`, `CyrusPlan`.
- **Logic in `lib/cyrus/tokens/`:**
  - Settings and the token rules.
  - The ledger: hold tokens when a build starts, charge the actual cost when it finishes, return the rest; spend the soonest-expiring tokens first.
  - Grants, build gating, Stripe billing, the worker sweep, and admin actions.
- **API:** routes under `/api/cyrus/tokens`, all limited to preview accounts.
- **Hooks into existing code:**
  - Grants run inside `placeGameOrder`, `commitRenewal` and `renewNow`, keyed per server and billing period so they can't double-grant.
  - Stripe webhooks go through `handleCyrusStripeEvent`.
  - A `cyrus-tokens` worker sweep runs every 5 minutes and re-syncs plans with Stripe hourly.
- **Wallet safety:** Cyrus checkouts carry `cyrusUserId`, never `nxeonUserId`, so the existing wallet/order fulfilment ignores them (a test pins this).
- **Admin page `/admin/cyrus-tokens`:** outstanding tokens and what they'd cost, spend against real AI cost, plans and monthly revenue, accounts, the ledger, grant/revoke/free-tier forms, and every setting.
- **Gating:** the setting `cyrus_tok_live` is `false`, so only preview accounts take part. The checkout line returns 404 for everyone else, including while impersonating.

## Stripe test-mode proof (real Stripe test API, test clock)

- I created the three plan prices with `scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts`. Re-running it changes nothing, and it refuses live keys.
- The balance through each step:

| Step | Balance |
|---|---|
| First month | 750 |
| Real renewal | 1,500 (stacked) |
| All real events replayed twice | still 1,500 |
| Upgrade to All models (real proration charge) | 10,202 |
| Real refund, processed twice | 9,452 |

- Cancel worked: the plan's tokens got their 30-day grace expiry.
- Log: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/proof-testclock.log`.
- This run caught a real bug in my first rollover design: re-processing an old invoice expired 7,202 tokens the customer had paid for. I switched to the 3-month-per-month expiry above and added a regression test; the re-run is clean.

## Hook points into Cyrus (one line each)

- `components/cyrus/CyrusApp.tsx`:
  - `<CyrusTokenChip />` in the home header.
  - `<CyrusTokensHost />`.
  - In `create()`: `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError(j)` and `cyrusTokens.refresh()`.
- `components/cyrus/Project.tsx`: `<CyrusTokenChip compact />`.
- `components/cyrus/Composer.tsx`:
  - `<CyrusTokenEstimate />` replaces the USD estimate.
  - `<CyrusModelLock />` in the model list.
  - `<CyrusModelPanelFoot />` replaces the "nothing is charged" footer.
- `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`: `<CyrusCheckoutLine />` in the game order summary.
- Outside the UI: the build-create route, `syncBuild` in `lib/modbuilder/store.ts`, the Stripe webhook, and the worker sweep.

## Owner decisions

1. Token value: 500 tokens per $1 of AI cost, Yakko 1.25x.
2. Server grant formula and 90-day expiry. Should grants go to Minecraft servers only?
3. Plan amounts (750 / 3,500 / 10,000), 3-month token life, 30-day grace after cancel.
4. The $4.99 Katara plan unlocks no new model, because free accounts already have Katara. Keep it as a cheap token pack, or add something to it?
5. Top-ups: 120 tokens/$, from $5 to $100.
6. 3 free failures per 7 days.
7. Daily caps of 5,000 and 1,000.
8. Saka currently maps to Sonnet 5, but Sonnet 5.5 was cheaper and better in the eval. Haiku (Katara) was not cheaper per build than Sonnet 5.5.
9. Going live:
   - Create the live prices with the setup script (`CYRUS_STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE=1 … --live`).
   - Enable `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.*` and `charge.refunded` on the live webhook.
   - Flip `cyrus_tok_live` to true.
10. Pass a per-build AI budget to the build service, so one build can never cost more than the tokens held for it.

**Act on this when merging:** spending is enforced by default, and the owner's balance starts at 0. After the merge he can't build in Cyrus until he grants himself tokens or a free tier at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`, or sets `cyrus_tok_enforce=false`. Prod also has no Cyrus Stripe prices yet, so plans will show "Coming soon" there.

## Housekeeping

- Throwaway database: `nxeon_agt_cyrustokens`; no cluster-wide commands.
- The worktree has its own node_modules and Prisma client.
- Commits list files explicitly.
- I removed the temporary worktree I used for comparing tests against `main`.

20646:**v4: the owner's concept (2026-10-07, same branch; replaces v3's look).** Concept: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/owner-concept.png`; log + side-by-sides: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/` (ROUNDS.md, compare/, best/). Cyrus fills the content area of the normal portal frame (the portal's own sidebar and top bar stay; an earlier "immersive" redraw of the portal chrome was reverted on the owner's call). Inside Cyrus, a top-left **switcher** (`components/cyrus/Switcher.tsx`) holds the projects per game (registry), Custom Project (template library) and the Cyrus Pro card (an upgrade CTA that explains Pro arrives with the token plans), plus Find (P) and New (N). Cyrus does not bind Ctrl K (the portal palette owns it). **The web** is a new engine: `web/tree-layout.ts` (pure, tested) lays out Cyrus core -> game (registry, Minecraft live, ARK / The Isle / Palworld / Rust / Valheim soon, + Add Game) -> category (`lib/cyrus/categories.ts`, deterministic keyword classifier with an "Other" fallback) -> mods (the user's projects, 3 per category + "+N more"; empty categories show templates marked TEMPLATE and a "New … mod" chip that prefills the composer); `web/tree.ts` draws the deep-navy space, drifting aurora ribbons, stars, the neon threads (per-branch hues, S-curves, beads) and travelling light (ambient trickle, brighter on the selected branch, streaming on running builds and on real build events), and moves a DOM layer of real buttons (`Stage.tsx`). **Inspector** (`Inspector.tsx`): Share (copies the link), more menu (jar, source zip, duplicate, copy request, stop), Deploy Mod (= the install modal); tabs Code (path + file switcher + live/final source) / Explain / Versions / Files (folders relative to the plugin package) / Notes; the mod card (category cube, title, version + loader chips, description or the live build stage track, failure verdict with retry, Open Project = zoom to the mod + Files, Download, View on NxLabs disabled until publishing exists) and Related Files. **Composer**: Chat / Generate / Debug / Refactor / Docs; Generate starts a new mod, the others build the next version of the selected mod with the request framed for the mode (`frameRequest` in Composer.tsx); attach, screenshot (getDisplayMedia, one frame), voice, Katara / Saka / Yakko. No "web search" toggle (the builder has no web access). **Icons** (`icons.tsx`): one set, Lucide geometry (ISC notice in the file) drawn with neon gradient strokes + glow (`tone`), original game emblems (NOT official logos: pixel grass cube, stylised A, raptor head, fox-like creature, bolted plate, V rune), isometric category-tinted mod cubes, and the real Nxeon X as the Cyrus mark. Colours are eyedropped from the concept (teal #3ce4dd, magenta-violet #cd4aff, violet #b81afa, cyan #2ed8ec, electric blue #0770fe -> #571af9 core, navy ground #020719) and the threads render as additive bloom (halo + glow + saturated line + white core) with white-cored beads. Light theme: the space canvas stays dark (the concept is neon in space); the switcher, inspector, composer and modals turn light.

input.content:
# Cyrus tokens: UI integration contract

How any Cyrus UI (current v4, or the owner's from-scratch redesign) plugs in the token
economy. Everything lives in `components/cyrus-tokens/` (branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`) and is
self-contained: its own store, styles (`tokens.css`, `cyt-*` classes) and Stripe payment form.
A new UI needs only the mounts below. Every component renders **nothing** for accounts outside
the token economy (not live and not a preview account), so mounting them is always safe.

Import everything from `@/components/cyrus-tokens`.

## Mounts (one line each)

| What | Mount | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| `<CyrusTokensHost />` | once, anywhere inside the Cyrus page. Owns the tokens modal (Plans / Top up / History), the inline Stripe card form, and the "Payment received" notice after the Stripe return (`?tokens=ok|pending`). Portals to `<body>`. | **yes** |
| `<CyrusTokenChip compact? beta? />` | header / switcher area. Balance + "Get more"; opens the modal on Plans. Low-balance state built in. | yes (one place) |

Hooks, all one line and minimal since the UI is being redesigned: in `Switcher.tsx` a token chip next to New plus a "Tokens & history" row; Cyrus Pro "Upgrade" opens the plans; in `Composer.tsx` the token estimate, model locks and picker footer; in `CyrusApp.tsx` the modal host and build-error handling. In the build route and `store.ts`, both my token hooks and the new mod-hooks are kept.
New-UI wiring contract (props, `cyrusTokens` API, routes, error codes): `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/UI-CONTRACT.md`. I did not restyle the token components; I only fixed one real v4 type break (the model colour field is gone, so they use their own colours now).
The full-repo `tsc` now runs out of memory at the 3 GB heap even inside the lock with more than 6 GB free, so I typechecked a scoped config instead: the 39 files this branch changes against b9 plus everything they import, which is clean. A full check at merge time needs a larger heap.
Tests, all run inside the lock: token + Cyrus + cyrus-mods + modbuilder 75/75, token DB 21/21. No E2E, deploy or merge to main.
